title: Fortidsvaner med pleide å — past habits
goal: Use pleide å for recurring past behavior, not one finished event.

objectives.statement: Use pleide å for recurring past behavior, not one finished event.

spans.value: Maja has recently returned to the town where she grew up. She meets her childhood friend Jonas near the river.
Da jeg bodde her, pleide jeg å sykle langs elva hver morgen.

blocks.translation: When I lived here, I used to cycle along the river every morning.

spans.value: Ja, og du pleide å vente på meg ved den gamle brua.

blocks.translation: Yes, and you used to wait for me by the old bridge.

spans.value: Vi pleide å kjøpe is i kiosken etter skolen også.

blocks.translation: We used to buy ice cream at the kiosk after school too.

spans.value: Det stemmer. Eieren pleide å kjenne alle barna i området.

blocks.translation: That’s right. The owner used to know all the children in the area.

spans.value: I går syklet jeg langs elva igjen.

blocks.translation: Yesterday I cycled along the river again.

spans.value: Stoppet du ved kiosken?

blocks.translation: Did you stop at the kiosk?

spans.value: Ja, jeg kjøpte en is. Men den gamle eieren jobber ikke der nå.

blocks.translation: Yes, I bought an ice cream. But the old owner doesn’t work there now.

spans.value: Maja and Jonas talk about two kinds of past experience. First, they remember routines from their childhood: cycling by the river, waiting at the bridge, and buying ice cream after school. These things happened regularly over a period of time. Then Maja describes what she did yesterday: she cycled, stopped, and bought one ice cream on one finished occasion.
That difference is the focus of this chapter.

sections.title: Saying what someone used to do

spans.value: Use
pleide å
when you want to present an action as a recurring past behavior or old routine.

no.value: Maja pleide å sykle langs elva.

en.value: Maja used to cycle along the river.

spans.value: The construction has three parts:
subject + pleide å + infinitive
In the example above:

items.value: pleide places the routine in the past.
sykle is the infinitive (infinitiv), the basic verb form.

spans.value: The same pattern works with different subjects:

no.value: Jeg pleide å gå til skolen.

en.value: I used to walk to school.

no.value: Han pleide å lage middag på søndager.

en.value: He used to make dinner on Sundays.

no.value: Vi pleide å besøke bestemor hver sommer.

en.value: We used to visit Grandma every summer.

no.value: Barna pleide å leke ute etter skolen.

en.value: The children used to play outside after school.

spans.value: The form
pleide
does not change with the subject:

no.value: Jeg pleide å lese før jeg la meg.

en.value: I used to read before going to bed.

no.value: De pleide å lese før de la seg.

en.value: They used to read before going to bed.

spans.value: A compact rule is:

statement.value: Use pleide å + infinitive to describe something that happened regularly during a past period.

spans.value: Words and phrases such as these often support that meaning:

items.value: da jeg var liten — when I was little

spans.value: These expressions do not create the grammar by themselves, but they help establish a recurring situation.

no.value: Da jeg var liten, pleide jeg å besøke tante Liv hver sommer.

en.value: When I was little, I used to visit Aunt Liv every summer.

no.value: Før pleide Amir å ta bussen til jobb.

en.value: Amir used to take the bus to work before.

no.value: Vi pleide å spise sammen på fredager.

en.value: We used to eat together on Fridays.

sections.title: A routine, not one finished event

spans.value: Compare these pairs carefully.

sections.title: A repeated journey and one completed journey

no.value: Før pleide Nora å gå til jobb.

en.value: Nora used to walk to work before.

no.value: I går gikk Nora til jobb.

en.value: Yesterday Nora walked to work.

spans.value: The first sentence describes Nora’s former routine. The second reports one completed journey yesterday.

no.value: Vi pleide å besøke bestemor hver søndag.

en.value: We used to visit Grandma every Sunday.

no.value: Vi besøkte bestemor på søndag.

en.value: We visited Grandma on Sunday.

spans.value: The regular visits belong with
pleide å
. The single Sunday visit is expressed with the ordinary past tense (preteritum), which you already know.

sections.title: A former evening habit and one evening

no.value: Erik pleide å lese før han la seg.

en.value: Erik used to read before going to bed.

no.value: Erik leste ferdig boka i går kveld.

en.value: Erik finished the book last night.

spans.value: The first sentence presents reading as Erik’s routine. The second tells us about one finished event.
The important question is not simply, Did this happen in the past? Both forms refer to the past. Ask instead:

statement.value: Am I presenting this as a regular behavior over a past period, or as one finished event?

spans.value: Use
pleide å
for the regular behavior. Do not use it merely because a sentence contains a past-time expression.

no.value: I fjor pleide vi å dra på hytta hver helg.

en.value: Last year we used to go to the cabin every weekend.

no.value: I fjor dro vi på hytta én gang.

en.value: Last year we went to the cabin once.

spans.value: Both sentences contain
i fjor
, but only the first describes a habit.

sections.title: More than once does not always mean a habit

spans.value: A habit is a repeated behavior connected to a period or routine. An action can happen several times during one finished occasion without becoming a habit.

no.value: Da jeg studerte, pleide jeg å ringe mamma hver søndag.

en.value: When I was a student, I used to call Mum every Sunday.

no.value: I går ringte jeg mamma tre ganger.

en.value: Yesterday I called Mum three times.

spans.value: Three calls are more than one call, but they all belong to one finished day. The second sentence does not describe an established routine.
Compare another pair:

no.value: Sara pleide å kjøpe kaffe på vei til jobb.

en.value: Sara used to buy coffee on her way to work.

no.value: I morges kjøpte Sara to kopper kaffe.

en.value: This morning Sara bought two cups of coffee.

spans.value: Two cups do not make the event a past habit. The time frame is one particular morning.

sections.title: Keep the next verb in the infinitive

spans.value: After
pleide å
, use the infinitive. Do not put the second verb in the past tense.

no.value: Hun pleide å gå hjem etter skolen.

en.value: She used to walk home after school.

no.value: Hun pleide å gikk hjem etter skolen.

en.value: She used to walked home after school.

spans.value: The past meaning is already carried by
pleide
. The verb after
å
remains in its infinitive form.

no.value: Vi pleide å spise middag klokka fem.

en.value: We used to eat dinner at five o’clock.

no.value: Vi pleide spiste middag klokka fem.

en.value: We used ate dinner at five o’clock.

spans.value: Do not omit
å
either:

no.value: Jonas pleide å vente ved brua.

en.value: Jonas used to wait by the bridge.

no.value: Jonas pleide vente ved brua.

en.value: Jonas used to wait by the bridge.

spans.value: For this lesson, remember the construction as one unit:
pleide å + infinitive
A sentence with
pleide å
often suggests that the old routine has changed or ended. Context usually makes this clearer.

no.value: Før pleide jeg å ta toget til jobb, men nå jobber jeg hjemme.

en.value: I used to take the train to work, but now I work from home.

no.value: Lea pleide å spille håndball, men nå spiller hun fotball.

en.value: Lea used to play handball, but now she plays football.

no.value: Vi pleide å møtes hver fredag. Nå bor vi i forskjellige byer.

en.value: We used to meet every Friday. Now we live in different cities.

spans.value: The essential meaning remains recurring past behavior. A contrast with the present can make the old-routine meaning especially natural, but you do not need to add a present-day contrast every time.

no.value: Bestefar pleide å fortelle morsomme historier.

en.value: Grandpa used to tell funny stories.

spans.value: This is complete even without a sentence about the present.
After their walk, Maja and Jonas sit outside the old kiosk.
Husker du parken bak skolen?

blocks.translation: Do you remember the park behind the school?

spans.value: Ja. Vi pleide å spille fotball der etter skolen.

blocks.translation: Yes. We used to play football there after school.

spans.value: Og du pleide å ta med appelsiner til alle.

blocks.translation: And you used to bring oranges for everyone.

spans.value: Det gjorde jeg! I går gikk jeg gjennom parken, men ingen spilte fotball.

blocks.translation: I did! Yesterday I walked through the park, but nobody was playing football.

spans.value: Ting forandrer seg.
The old football games and the oranges were part of a repeated routine. Maja’s walk yesterday was one finished event. The same contrast from the opening dialogue still applies.
Using pleide å for one dated event

no.value: I går pleide jeg å møte Jonas på kafeen.

en.value: Yesterday I used to meet Jonas at the café. (for the intended meaning)

spans.value: If there was one meeting yesterday, use a finished past event:

no.value: I går møtte jeg Jonas på kafeen.

en.value: Yesterday I met Jonas at the café.

spans.value: Use
pleide å
only if meeting Jonas was a recurring past practice:

no.value: Før pleide jeg å møte Jonas på kafeen hver torsdag.

en.value: I used to meet Jonas at the café every Thursday.

spans.value: Putting two past forms together

no.value: Vi pleide å kjøpte is etter skolen.

en.value: We used to bought ice cream after school.

spans.value: Correct:

no.value: Vi pleide å kjøpe is etter skolen.

en.value: We used to buy ice cream after school.

spans.value: Choosing by time word alone
A phrase such as
i fjor
can introduce either a routine or a finished event.

no.value: I fjor pleide jeg å svømme hver morgen.

en.value: Last year I used to swim every morning.

no.value: I fjor svømte jeg over fjorden én gang.

en.value: Last year I swam across the fjord once.

spans.value: Read the whole situation. Look for recurring behavior, not merely a reference to the past.
Imagine that Henrik has returned to the neighborhood where he lived while studying. He wants to explain his old weekday routine and then report one thing he did during today’s visit.

prompt.value: Choose the interpretation that fits the dialogue.

options.text: All four activities are former routines that Maja used to repeat regularly.
options.why: The last line places the cycling and the ice-cream purchase on one specific day, «i går», not in a recurring past period.

options.text: The three childhood activities are former routines, while yesterday's cycling and ice-cream purchase are finished events from one visit.
options.why: «Pleide å» marks the repeated childhood activities, and «i går» reports one finished visit.

options.text: All four activities are single finished events, three from childhood and one from yesterday.
options.why: The first three lines use «pleide å», which presents repeated childhood habits rather than one-off events.

text.value: «Da jeg bodde her, pleide jeg å sykle langs elva hver morgen.»
«Du pleide å vente på meg ved den gamle brua.»
«Vi pleide å kjøpe is etter skolen også.»
«I går syklet jeg langs elva igjen og kjøpte en is.»

prompt.value: Build the sentence about what the group used to do together on weekends.

explanation.value: «Pleide» uttrykker fortid, og verbet etter «å» står i infinitiv.

text.value: «Hva gjorde dere sammen i helgene før?»
Gruppa hadde en fast leserutine i helgene.

prompt.value: Choose the pair that fits both situations.

options.text: «En dag kjøpte Sara kaffe på vei til jobb. I morges kjøpte Sara to kopper kaffe.»
options.why: Den første setningen beskriver én bestemt anledning, ikke en gjentatt vane.

options.text: «Sara pleide å kjøpe kaffe på vei til jobb. I morges pleide Sara å kjøpe to kopper kaffe.»
options.why: Den andre setningen gjelder én bestemt morgen, så den kan ikke uttrykke en etablert vane.

options.text: «Sara pleide å kjøpe kaffe på vei til jobb. I morges kjøpte Sara to kopper kaffe.»
options.why: Den første setningen beskriver en vane som gjentok seg i en tidligere periode, mens den andre forteller hva som skjedde i morges.

text.value: «Var kaffebaren et fast stopp på vei til jobb før?»
«Ja, hver arbeidsdag i flere år.»
«Hva med i morges?»
«Da ble det to kopper kaffe.»

prompt.value: Choose the pair that distinguishes an action that happened several times yesterday from an old habit.

explanation.value: At en handling gjentas én dag, gjør den ikke automatisk til en gammel vane. En aktivitet hver søndag over flere år beskriver en rutine.

options.text: «I går flyttet jeg og ringte mamma flere ganger. Bestefar fikk telefon fra meg hver søndag i barndommen.»
options.why: Meldingene om gårsdagen beskriver én avgrenset dag, mens søndagstelefonene var en tidligere rutine.

options.text: «I går pleide jeg å ringe mamma tre ganger. Før ringte jeg bestefar hver søndag.»
options.why: Pleide å wrongly treats the three calls yesterday as a former routine.

options.text: «I går pleide jeg å ringe mamma tre ganger. Før pleide jeg å ringe bestefar hver søndag.»
options.why: The Sunday calls were a routine; yesterday's calls were one finished occasion.

options.text: «I går ringer jeg mamma tre ganger. Før pleide jeg å ringe bestefar hver søndag.»
options.why: The calls yesterday need a past-tense report.

text.value: I går ringte jeg mamma tre ganger mens jeg flyttet. Da jeg var barn, ringte jeg bestefar hver søndag i flere år.

prompt.value: Find the verb form that is incorrect.

payload.feedback: Etter «pleide å» bruker vi infinitiv: «gå». «Pleide» viser allerede til fortiden.

text.value: «Hvordan kom hun seg hjem etter skolen før?»
«Hun pleide å gikk hjem etter skolen.»

prompt.value: Write a reply from Maja to Jonas. Say what they used to do in the summer, include that Jonas usually brought juice, and distinguish the routines from the one bike ride Maja took yesterday.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate childhood-cycling, childhood-lemonade, yesterday-ride, and contrast-forms as gating criteria. Accept natural Norwegian wording that reports the two old routines, using «pleide å» for at least one of them, and yesterday's single ride with ordinary past tense.

criteria.instruction: Reports that Maja and Jonas regularly cycled to the lake in childhood summers.
Reports that Jonas usually brought saft on those trips.
Reports that Maja syklet én gang forbi innsjøen i går.

Uses pleide å with infinitive for at least one former routine and a natural past-tense form for yesterday's single event; the other routine may use pleide å or a natural habitual past such as «som regel» with a preteritum form.

text.value: «Husker du somrene ved innsjøen?»
Da de var barn, syklet Maja og Jonas ofte til innsjøen om sommeren. Jonas tok som regel med saft.
«Kom du forbi innsjøen i går?»
Maja syklet én gang forbi innsjøen i går.

prompt.value: Write a message from Henrik to Nora in your own words. Include these routines from his student days: he took the bus to campus every weekday, ate soup at the student café on Fridays, studied at the library every evening, and played chess with Ali afterwards. Use «pleide å» at least once for a routine; express the other routines naturally. Also say that he walked to campus once today.

payload.judge_prompt: Check criteria recurring-habits, finished-event, independent-transfer, event-form-observation, and comprehensibility as gating criteria. Accept natural Bokmål variants and report evidence for every criterion id.

criteria.instruction: The message presents all four supplied activities as recurring routines from Henrik's student years. It uses «pleide å» followed by an infinitive for at least one routine; the others may use «pleide å» or natural habitual past-tense wording.
The message reports Henrik's single walk to campus during today's visit.
The response uses the learner's own wording and does not copy a complete sentence from the lesson.
The distinction between Henrik's former routines and today's visit is understandable.
The message expresses today's single finished action with an ordinary past-tense form, not «pleide å».

text.value: Henrik har kommet tilbake til det gamle studentstrøket sitt og skriver til venninnen Nora.

prompt.value: Choose the message that fits both details.

options.text: «Ida pleide å svømme før skolen hver mandag. Sist mandag pleide hun å krysse innsjøen én gang.»
options.why: A single dated lake crossing is not an established past routine.

options.text: «Ida pleide å svømme før skolen hver mandag. Sist mandag svømte hun over innsjøen én gang.»
options.why: The weekly activity is a former routine, while the lake crossing is one finished event.

options.text: «Ida pleide å krysse innsjøen hver mandag i skoleårene. Sist mandag svømte hun én gang før skolen.»
options.why: This swaps the two facts: the weekly school-year routine was the morning swim, while the lake crossing happened once, last Monday.

text.value: «Hva var Idas faste rutine før i tiden?»
«Hun tok en svømmetur hver mandag før undervisningen.»
«Og hva skjedde sist mandag?»
«Da svømte hun over innsjøen for første gang.»

prompt.value: Choose the reply with the correct verb form.

options.text: «Vi pleide å besøkte henne hver uke.»
options.why: The second verb cannot remain in the past tense because «pleide» already carries the past meaning.
The taught construction requires the infinitive marker between «pleide» and the infinitive.

options.text: «Vi pleide å besøke henne hver uke.»
options.why: The construction contains «pleide», the infinitive marker «å», and the infinitive «besøke».

text.value: «Hva gjorde dere vanligvis hos bestemor om sommeren?»
De besøkte henne hver uke.
